source.text: בִּשְׁנַת֙ שְׁבַֽע־עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה לְפֶ֖קַח בֶּן־רְמַלְיָ֑הוּ מָלַ֛ךְ אָחָ֥ז בֶּן־יוֹתָ֖ם מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: In [the] year seventeen year of Pekah son of Remaliah reigned Ahaz son of Jotham king of Judah.

en.L: In the seventeenth year of Pekah son of Remaliah, Ahaz son of Jotham, king of Judah, reigned.
en.B: In the seventeenth year of Pekah son of Remaliah, Ahaz son of Jotham became king of Judah.
en.R: Ahaz son of Jotham became king of Judah. It was the seventeenth year that Pekah son of Remaliah had been king of Israel.

es.L: En el año diecisiete de Peka hijo de Remalías, reinó Acaz hijo de Jotam, rey de Judá.
es.B: En el año diecisiete de Peka hijo de Remalías, Acaz hijo de Jotam comenzó a reinar en Judá.
es.R: Acaz hijo de Jotam comenzó a reinar en Judá. Era el año diecisiete del reinado de Peka hijo de Remalías en Israel.

fr.L: En la dix-septième année de Péqah fils de Remalia, Achaz fils de Jotham, roi de Juda, régna.
fr.B: La dix-septième année du règne de Péqah, fils de Remalia, Achaz, fils de Jotham, devint roi de Juda.
fr.R: Achaz fils de Jotham est devenu roi de Juda. C’était la dix-septième année du règne de Péqah fils de Remalia, roi d’Israël.

sw.L: Katika mwaka wa kumi na saba wa Peka mwana wa Remalia, Ahazi mwana wa Yothamu, mfalme wa Yuda, alitawala.
sw.B: Katika mwaka wa kumi na saba wa Peka mwana wa Remalia, Ahazi mwana wa Yothamu alianza kutawala Yuda.
sw.R: Ahazi mwana wa Yothamu alianza kutawala Yuda. Ilikuwa katika mwaka wa kumi na saba wa utawala wa Peka mwana wa Remalia mfalme wa Israeli.

vi.L: Năm thứ mười bảy đời Phê-ca con trai Rê-ma-lia, A-cha con trai Giô-tham vua Giu-đa trị vì.
vi.B: Năm thứ mười bảy đời Phê-ca con trai Rê-ma-lia, A-cha con trai Giô-tham lên làm vua Giu-đa.
vi.R: A-cha con trai Giô-tham lên làm vua Giu-đa. Lúc ấy là năm thứ mười bảy đời Phê-ca con trai Rê-ma-lia làm vua Y-sơ-ra-ên.

ko.L: 르말랴의 아들 베가의 제17년에 유다 왕 요담의 아들 아하스가 왕이 되었다.
ko.B: 르말랴의 아들 베가가 다스린 지 17년째 되는 해에 유다 왕 요담의 아들 아하스가 왕이 되었다.
ko.R: 요담의 아들 아하스가 유다의 왕이 되었다. 그때는 르말랴의 아들 베가가 이스라엘의 왕이 된 지 17년째 되는 해였다.

pt.L: No décimo sétimo ano de Peca, filho de Remalias, Acaz, filho de Jotão, rei de Judá, reinou.
pt.B: No décimo sétimo ano de Peca, filho de Remalias, Acaz, filho de Jotão, começou a reinar sobre Judá.
pt.R: Acaz, filho de Jotão, se tornou rei de Judá. Foi no décimo sétimo ano em que Peca, filho de Remalias, era rei de Israel.

am.L: በሮሜልዩ ልጅ በፋቁሔ በአሥራ ሰባተኛው ዓመት የይሁዳ ንጉሥ የኢዮአታም ልጅ አካዝ ነገሠ።
am.B: የሮሜልዩ ልጅ ፋቁሔ በነገሠ በአሥራ ሰባተኛው ዓመት የኢዮአታም ልጅ አካዝ በይሁዳ ላይ ነገሠ።
am.R: የኢዮአታም ልጅ አካዝ የይሁዳ ንጉሥ ሆነ። ይህም የሮሜልዩ ልጅ ፋቁሔ በእስራኤል በነገሠ በአሥራ ሰባተኛው ዓመት ነበረ።

hi.L: रमल्याह के पुत्र पेकह के सत्रहवें वर्ष में यहूदा के राजा योताम का पुत्र आहाज़ राज्य करने लगा।
hi.B: रमल्याह के पुत्र पेकह के सत्रहवें वर्ष में योताम का पुत्र आहाज़ यहूदा का राजा बना।
hi.R: इस्राएल के राजा रमल्याह के पुत्र पेकह के राज्य के सत्रहवें वर्ष में योताम का बेटा आहाज़ यहूदा का राजा बना।

ru.L: В семнадцатый год Факея, сына Ремалии, воцарился Ахаз, сын Иоафама, царь Иудейский.
ru.B: В семнадцатый год Факея, сына Ремалии, воцарился Ахаз, сын Иоафама, царь Иудейский.
ru.R: Ахаз, сын Иоафама, стал царём Иуды. Это был семнадцатый год царствования Факея, сына Ремалии, царя Израиля.

ja.L: レマルヤの子ペカの第十七年に、ユダの王ヨタムの子アハズが王となった。
ja.B: レマルヤの子ペカの治世第十七年に、ヨタムの子アハズがユダの王となった。
ja.R: ヨタムの息子アハズが、ユダの王になりました。それは、レマルヤの息子ペカがイスラエルの王になって十七年目のことでした。

uk.L: У сімнадцятому році Пекаха, сина Ремалії, зацарював Ахаз, син Йоатама, цар Юдеї.
uk.B: У сімнадцятому році Пекаха, сина Ремалії, Ахаз, син Йоатама, став царем Юдеї.
uk.R: Ахаз, син Йоатама, став царем Юдеї. Це був сімнадцятий рік царювання Пекаха, сина Ремалії, над Ізраїлем.

decisions.choice: dated by the reign of Pekah, king of Israel
decisions.reason: As throughout Kings, the start of a reign in Judah is dated by the year of the king ruling in Israel (1 Kings 15:1). Pekah had seized the throne of Israel in Samaria (15:25). Ahaz's reign is told in verses 1-20, and again in 2 Chronicles 28.

decisions.choice: Ahaz ... king of Judah: the title belongs to Ahaz
decisions.reason: "King of Judah" describes Ahaz, who now begins to reign, not his father Jotham. The verb "reigned" with a date marks the start of the reign, as in 1 Kings 15:1.

decisions.choice: Ahaz son of Jotham: the king of Isaiah 7
decisions.reason: This is the Ahaz whom the prophet Isaiah met in the crisis of verse 5 (Isaiah 7:1-17), and to whom he gave the sign of Immanuel.

decisions.choice: two sentences, the date second
decisions.reason: Readable splits the formula into two sentences, as these books allow, and says that Pekah was king of Israel.

decisions.choice: Acaz, filho de Jotão; Peca, filho de Remalias; the synchronism worded as 1 Kings 15:1
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the kings take the forms of the shared list for Kings, "Acaz" and "Peca", and the father "Jotão" and "Remalias", as the chapters before give them. The synchronism keeps the wording 1 Kings 15:1 set at each level, the year as an ordinal ("décimo sétimo"), "começou a reinar" at Balanced and "se tornou rei" at Readable.

decisions.choice: No gender spans in the Amharic of 2 Kings 16: "የእስራኤል ልጆች" (Literal, Balanced) and "እስራኤላውያን" (Readable) in verse 3.
decisions.reason: The Amharic words already include women, as in 2 Kings 17 and 21.

decisions.choice: "アハズ" for Ahaz (MAT 1:9)
decisions.reason: The NT form of the name.

source.text: בֶּן־עֶשְׂרִ֤ים שָׁנָה֙ אָחָ֣ז בְּמָלְכ֔וֹ וְשֵׁשׁ־עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְלֹא־עָשָׂ֣ה הַיָּשָׁ֗ר בְּעֵינֵ֛י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהָ֖יו כְּדָוִ֥ד אָבִֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: A son of twenty year[s] [was] Ahaz when he became king, and sixteen year[s] he reigned in Jerusalem; and not he did the right in [the] eyes of Yahweh his God like David his father.

en.L: Ahaz [was] twenty years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. And he did not do the right in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God, like David his father.
en.B: Ahaz was twenty years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. He did not do what was right in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God, as his ancestor David had done.
en.R: Ahaz was twenty years old when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for sixteen years. He did not do what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God said was right, as his ancestor David had done.

es.L: Acaz [tenía] veinte años cuando comenzó a reinar, y reinó dieciséis años en Jerusalén. Y no hizo lo recto a los ojos {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} su Dios, como David su padre.
es.B: Acaz tenía veinte años cuando comenzó a reinar, y reinó dieciséis años en Jerusalén. No hizo lo recto a los ojos {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} su Dios, como lo había hecho su antepasado David.
es.R: Acaz tenía veinte años cuando llegó a ser rey, y gobernó en Jerusalén durante dieciséis años. No hizo lo que agrada {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} su Dios, como lo había hecho su antepasado David.

fr.L: Achaz avait vingt ans quand il devint roi, et il régna seize ans à Jérusalem. Et il ne fit pas ce qui est droit aux yeux {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} son Dieu, comme David son père.
fr.B: Achaz avait vingt ans quand il devint roi, et il régna seize ans à Jérusalem. Il ne fit pas ce qui est juste aux yeux {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} son Dieu, comme l’avait fait son ancêtre David.
fr.R: Achaz avait vingt ans quand il est devenu roi, et il a régné à Jérusalem pendant seize ans. Il n’a pas fait ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} son Dieu déclare bon, comme l’avait fait son ancêtre David.

sw.L: Ahazi [alikuwa] mwana wa miaka ishirini alipoanza kutawala, naye alitawala miaka kumi na sita huko Yerusalemu. Wala hakufanya yaliyo sawa machoni pa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wake, kama Daudi baba yake.
sw.B: Ahazi alikuwa na umri wa miaka ishirini alipoanza kutawala, naye akatawala miaka kumi na sita huko Yerusalemu. Hakufanya yaliyo sawa machoni pa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wake, kama babu yake Daudi alivyofanya.
sw.R: Ahazi alikuwa na umri wa miaka ishirini alipoanza kutawala, naye akatawala huko Yerusalemu kwa miaka kumi na sita. Hakufanya yale {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wake aliyoyaona kuwa mema, kama babu yake Daudi alivyofanya.

vi.L: A-cha [được] hai mươi tuổi khi lên làm vua, và trị vì mười sáu năm tại Giê-ru-sa-lem. Ông không làm điều ngay thẳng trước mắt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của ông như Đa-vít tổ phụ ông.
vi.B: A-cha được hai mươi tuổi khi lên làm vua và trị vì mười sáu năm tại Giê-ru-sa-lem. Ông không làm điều ngay thẳng trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của ông như Đa-vít tổ tiên ông đã làm.
vi.R: A-cha được hai mươi tuổi khi lên làm vua, và ông cai trị tại Giê-ru-sa-lem mười sáu năm. Ông không làm điều {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của ông cho là phải, như Đa-vít tổ tiên ông đã làm.

ko.L: 아하스가 왕이 되었을 때 20세[였고], 예루살렘에서 16년 동안 다스렸다. 그리고 그는 그의 조상 다윗처럼 그의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 눈에 올바른 일을 하지 않았다.
ko.B: 아하스는 20세에 왕이 되어 예루살렘에서 16년 동안 다스렸다. 그는 그의 조상 다윗과 달리 그의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 보시기에 올바른 일을 하지 않았다.
ko.R: 아하스는 20세에 왕이 되었고, 예루살렘에서 16년 동안 다스렸다. 그는 그의 조상 다윗과 달리, 그의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 옳다고 하신 일을 하지 않았다.

pt.L: Acaz [tinha] vinte anos quando começou a reinar, e reinou dezesseis anos em Jerusalém. E não fez o reto aos olhos {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, o seu Deus, como Davi, seu pai.
pt.B: Acaz tinha vinte anos quando começou a reinar, e reinou dezesseis anos em Jerusalém. Ele não fez o que era reto aos olhos {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, o seu Deus, como o seu antepassado Davi tinha feito.
pt.R: Acaz tinha vinte anos quando se tornou rei, e governou dezesseis anos em Jerusalém. Ele não fez o que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, o seu Deus, considerava certo, como o seu antepassado Davi tinha feito.

am.L: አካዝም መንገሥ በጀመረ ጊዜ የሃያ ዓመት ሰው [ነበረ]፤ በኢየሩሳሌምም አሥራ ስድስት ዓመት ነገሠ። እንደ አባቱ እንደ ዳዊትም በአምላኩ {{divine_name:በእግዚአብሔር|በያህዌ}} ዓይን ቅን የሆነውን አላደረገም።
am.B: አካዝ መንገሥ በጀመረ ጊዜ ዕድሜው ሃያ ዓመት ነበር፤ በኢየሩሳሌምም አሥራ ስድስት ዓመት ነገሠ። አባቱ ዳዊት እንዳደረገው በአምላኩ {{divine_name:በእግዚአብሔር|በያህዌ}} ፊት ቅን የሆነውን አላደረገም።
am.R: አካዝ ንጉሥ በሆነ ጊዜ ሃያ ዓመቱ ነበር፤ በኢየሩሳሌምም አሥራ ስድስት ዓመት ገዛ። አባቱ ዳዊት እንዳደረገው አምላኩ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ትክክል ነው የሚለውን አላደረገም።

hi.L: जब आहाज़ राजा बना तब वह बीस वर्ष का था, और उसने यरूशलेम में सोलह वर्ष राज्य किया; और उसने अपने पिता दाऊद के समान वह नहीं किया जो {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} उसके परमेश्वर की दृष्टि में ठीक था।
hi.B: जब आहाज़ राजा बना तब वह बीस वर्ष का था, और उसने यरूशलेम में सोलह वर्ष राज्य किया। उसने अपने पूर्वज दाऊद के समान वह नहीं किया जो {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} उसके परमेश्वर की दृष्टि में ठीक था।
hi.R: जब आहाज़ राजा बना, तब वह बीस वर्ष का था। उसने यरूशलेम में सोलह वर्ष तक राज्य किया। उसने अपने पूर्वज दाऊद के समान वह नहीं किया जो {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} उसके परमेश्वर की दृष्टि में ठीक था।

ru.L: Двадцати лет [был] Ахаз, когда воцарился, и шестнадцать лет он царствовал в Иерусалиме. И не делал он того, что было правильным в глазах {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Яхве}}, его Бога, как Давид, его отец.
ru.B: Ахазу было двадцать лет, когда он воцарился, и шестнадцать лет он царствовал в Иерусалиме. Он не делал того, что было правильным в глазах {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Яхве}}, его Бога, как делал его предок Давид.
ru.R: Ахазу было двадцать лет, когда он стал царём. Он царствовал в Иерусалиме шестнадцать лет. Он не делал того, что нравилось {{divine_name:ГОСПОДУ|Яхве}}, его Богу, как делал его предок Давид.

ja.L: アハズは王となったとき二十歳で、エルサレムで十六年治めた。そして彼は、彼の父ダビデのようには、彼の神、{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}の目に正しいことを行わなかった。
ja.B: アハズは王となったとき二十歳で、エルサレムで十六年間治めた。彼は、先祖ダビデとは違って、自分の神、{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}の目に正しいとされることを行わなかった。
ja.R: アハズは二十歳で王になり、エルサレムで十六年間治めました。アハズは、先祖ダビデとは違って、自分の神である{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}が正しいと言われることをしませんでした。

uk.L: Ахазові [було] двадцять років, коли він зацарював, і шістнадцять років він царював у Єрусалимі. І не робив він правильного в очах {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Ягве}}, свого Бога, як Давид, його батько.
uk.B: Ахазові було двадцять років, коли він став царем, і він царював у Єрусалимі шістнадцять років. Він не робив того, що було правильне в очах {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Ягве}}, його Бога, як робив його предок Давид.
uk.R: Ахазові було двадцять років, коли він став царем, і він правив у Єрусалимі шістнадцять років. Він не робив того, що подобалося {{divine_name:ГОСПОДУ|Ягве}}, його Богові, як робив його предок Давид.

decisions.choice: a son of twenty years: twenty years old
decisions.reason: Hebrew gives a person's age as being "a son of" so many years.

decisions.choice: twenty years old, sixteen years: numbers hard to fit together
alternatives: twenty-five years old (some Greek copies of 2 Chronicles 28:1)
decisions.reason: Ahaz's son Hezekiah was twenty-five when he became king after him (18:2). If Ahaz was twenty at his accession and reigned sixteen years, he would have been about eleven when Hezekiah was born. Reigns that overlapped with a father's, or an error in copying one of the numbers, may explain this. 2 Chronicles 28:1 has the same numbers in Hebrew, but some ancient Greek copies there read twenty-five. Every level keeps the numbers of the Hebrew text; reviewers should check the evidence.

decisions.choice: no mother named
decisions.reason: The formula for a king of Judah usually names his mother (15:2, 33). For Ahaz it names none. The text gives no reason.

decisions.choice: he did not do what was right ... like David: the good verdict denied
decisions.reason: The verdict is the one given to the good kings of Judah (1 Kings 15:11), turned into a denial. His father Jotham and the kings before him had received the good verdict (15:3, 34). "David his father" means his ancestor David, the measure for every king of Judah.

decisions.choice: did not do the right in [the] eyes of / did not do what was right in the sight of / did not do what the LORD his God said was right; his ancestor
decisions.reason: The good verdict is worded the same way at each level throughout Kings, here with "not". Balanced and Readable say "ancestor" for "father", as they do wherever David is called the father of a later king.

decisions.choice: "no hizo lo recto a los ojos del SEÑOR" (L, B); "no hizo lo que agrada al SEÑOR" (R); "su antepasado David" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The good verdict keeps its fixed wording at each level, here with "no"; Balanced and Readable say "antepasado" where David is called the father of a later king.

decisions.choice: não fez o reto aos olhos do SENHOR (L); não fez o que era reto aos olhos do SENHOR (B); não fez o que o SENHOR ... considerava certo (R)
decisions.reason: The accession formula and the good verdict keep the wordings 1 Kings 14:21 and 15:11 set at each level, here with "não" (m4); no mother is named, as in the Hebrew (m3).

decisions.choice: "በአምላኩ {{divine_name:በእግዚአብሔር|በያህዌ}} ዓይን ቅን የሆነውን አላደረገም" (Literal); "... ፊት ..." (Balanced); "አምላኩ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ትክክል ነው የሚለውን አላደረገም" (Readable)
decisions.reason: The verdict formula in the negative, with "his God" before the name and the prefix on both words, as the Joshua-Samuel terms list sets for "the LORD your God". Literal brackets "[ነበረ]": the Hebrew has no verb in the age clause.

decisions.choice: не делал того, что было правильным в глазах ГОСПОДА (L, B); не делал того, что нравилось ГОСПОДУ (R)
decisions.reason: The good verdict is denied here (m4), and each level keeps its fixed wording of the verdict with "не"; Balanced and Readable say "предок" for David, as the English says "ancestor".

decisions.choice: The good verdict negated in its fixed form: "…の目に正しいことを行わなかった" (L), "…正しいとされることを行わなかった" (B), "…が正しいと言われることをしませんでした" (R)
decisions.reason: Keeps the refrain recognizable while stating that it is denied.

source.text: וַיֵּ֕לֶךְ בְּדֶ֖רֶךְ מַלְכֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְגַ֤ם אֶת־בְּנוֹ֙ הֶעֱבִ֣יר בָּאֵ֔שׁ כְּתֹֽעֲבוֹת֙ הַגּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֨ר הוֹרִ֤ישׁ יְהוָה֙ אֹתָ֔ם מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And he walked in [the] way of [the] kings of Israel, and even his son he made pass in the fire, according to [the] abominations of the nations whom dispossessed Yahweh from before [the] sons of Israel.

en.L: And he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, and he even made his son pass through the fire, according to the abominations of the nations whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had driven out before the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel.
en.B: He walked in the way of the kings of Israel. He even made his son pass through the fire, following the detestable practices of the nations that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had driven out ahead of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.
en.R: He lived the way the kings of Israel had lived. He even burned his own son in the fire as a sacrifice. He copied the disgusting practices of the nations that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had driven out of the land ahead of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

es.L: Y anduvo en el camino de los reyes de Israel, y aun hizo pasar a su hijo por el fuego, conforme a las abominaciones de las naciones que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había expulsado de delante de los hijos de Israel.
es.B: Anduvo en el camino de los reyes de Israel. Incluso hizo pasar a su hijo por el fuego, siguiendo las prácticas detestables de las naciones que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había expulsado de delante de los israelitas.
es.R: Vivió como habían vivido los reyes de Israel. Hasta quemó a su propio hijo en el fuego como sacrificio. Imitó las prácticas repugnantes de las naciones que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había echado de la tierra para dar lugar a los israelitas.

fr.L: Et il marcha dans la voie des rois d’Israël, et même il fit passer son fils par le feu, selon les abominations des nations que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avait dépossédées devant les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël.
fr.B: Il marcha dans la voie des rois d’Israël. Il alla jusqu’à faire passer son fils par le feu, selon les pratiques abominables des nations que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avait chassées devant les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}.
fr.R: Il a vécu comme les rois d’Israël. Il a même brûlé son propre fils dans le feu, en sacrifice. Il a imité les pratiques dégoûtantes des peuples que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avait chassés du pays devant les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}.

sw.L: Naye akaenda katika njia ya wafalme wa Israeli, hata mwanawe akampitisha motoni, sawasawa na machukizo ya mataifa ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliyafukuza mbele ya wana wa Israeli.
sw.B: Aliifuata njia ya wafalme wa Israeli. Hata alimpitisha mwanawe motoni, akifuata desturi za kuchukiza za mataifa ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliyafukuza mbele ya Waisraeli.
sw.R: Aliishi kama wafalme wa Israeli walivyoishi. Hata alimchoma mwanawe mwenyewe motoni kuwa dhabihu. Aliiga desturi za kuchukiza za mataifa ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliyafukuza kutoka katika nchi mbele ya Waisraeli.

vi.L: Ông đi theo đường lối của các vua Y-sơ-ra-ên, và còn cho con trai mình đi qua lửa, theo các điều ghê tởm của các dân tộc mà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã đuổi khỏi trước mặt con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.B: Ông đi theo đường lối của các vua Y-sơ-ra-ên. Ông còn cho con trai mình đi qua lửa, theo những thói ghê tởm của các dân tộc mà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã đuổi đi trước mặt dân Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.R: Ông sống theo cách các vua Y-sơ-ra-ên đã sống. Ông còn thiêu chính con trai mình trong lửa để làm sinh tế. Ông bắt chước những thói ghê tởm của các dân tộc mà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã đuổi ra khỏi xứ trước mặt dân Y-sơ-ra-ên.

ko.L: 그리고 그는 이스라엘 왕들의 길로 걸었고, 심지어 그의 아들을 불 가운데로 지나가게 했다. 이는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이스라엘 자손 앞에서 쫓아내신 민족들의 가증한 일들을 따른 것이었다.
ko.B: 그는 이스라엘 왕들의 길로 걸었다. 그는 심지어 자기 아들을 불 가운데로 지나가게 했다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이스라엘 자손 앞에서 쫓아내신 민족들의 역겨운 관습을 따른 것이다.
ko.R: 그는 이스라엘 왕들이 살던 대로 살았다. 그는 심지어 자기 아들을 불에 태워 제물로 바쳤다. 그는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이스라엘 사람들 앞에서 그 땅에서 쫓아내신 민족들의 끔찍한 풍습을 그대로 따랐다.

pt.L: E andou no caminho dos reis de Israel, e até fez o seu filho passar pelo fogo, conforme as abominações das nações que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} tinha expulsado de diante dos filhos de Israel.
pt.B: Ele andou no caminho dos reis de Israel. Até fez o seu filho passar pelo fogo, seguindo as coisas abomináveis das nações que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} tinha expulsado de diante dos israelitas.
pt.R: Ele viveu como os reis de Israel tinham vivido. Chegou a queimar o seu próprio filho no fogo como sacrifício. Imitou as coisas abomináveis que faziam as nações que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} tinha expulsado da terra para dar lugar aos israelitas.

am.L: በእስራኤልም ነገሥታት መንገድ ሄደ፤ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ከእስራኤል ልጆች ፊት እንዳሳደዳቸው እንደ ሕዝቦቹ አስጸያፊ ነገሮች ልጁን ደግሞ በእሳት አሳለፈ።
am.B: በእስራኤል ነገሥታት መንገድ ሄደ። {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ከእስራኤል ልጆች ፊት ያሳደዳቸው ሕዝቦች ያደርጉት የነበረውን አስጸያፊ ልማድ ተከትሎ ልጁን እንኳ በእሳት አሳለፈ።
am.R: የእስራኤል ነገሥታት እንደ ኖሩት ኖረ። የገዛ ልጁን እንኳ መሥዋዕት አድርጎ በእሳት አቃጠለ። {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ለእስራኤላውያን ሲል ከምድሪቱ ያባረራቸው ሕዝቦች ያደርጉት የነበረውን አስጸያፊ ልማድ ተከተለ።

hi.L: और वह इस्राएल के राजाओं की चाल चला, और उसने अपने पुत्र को भी आग में से पार कराया, उन जातियों के घृणित कामों के अनुसार जिन्हें {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} ने {{gender:इस्राएल की सन्तान|इस्राएल के पुत्रों}} के सामने से निकाल दिया था।
hi.B: वह इस्राएल के राजाओं की चाल चला। उसने अपने पुत्र को भी आग में से पार कराया, और उन जातियों के घृणित कामों पर चला जिन्हें {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} ने इस्राएलियों के आगे से निकाल दिया था।
hi.R: वह इस्राएल के राजाओं के जैसा जीवन जीता था। उसने अपने ही बेटे को बलि करके आग में जला दिया। उसने उन जातियों के घिनौने कामों की नक़ल की जिन्हें {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} ने इस्राएलियों के आगे से उस देश से निकाल दिया था।

ru.L: И ходил он путём царей Израиля, и даже сына своего провёл через огонь, по мерзостям народов, которых изгнал {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}} перед {{gender:детьми Израиля|сынами Израиля}}.
ru.B: Он ходил путём царей Израиля. Он даже провёл своего сына через огонь, следуя мерзким обычаям народов, которых {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}} изгнал перед израильтянами.
ru.R: Он жил так же, как жили цари Израиля. Он даже сжёг своего сына в огне как жертву. Он перенял отвратительные обычаи народов, которых {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}} прогнал из этой земли перед израильтянами.

ja.L: そして彼はイスラエルの王たちの道を歩み、さらに自分の子に火の中を通らせた。{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}がイスラエルの子らの前から追い払われた諸国民の忌むべき行いのとおりである。
ja.B: 彼はイスラエルの王たちの道を歩んだ。さらに、自分の息子に火の中を通らせることまでした。{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}がイスラエルの人々の前から追い払われた諸国民の、忌むべき習わしに倣ったのである。
ja.R: アハズは、イスラエルの王たちと同じように生きました。そのうえ、自分の息子を火で焼いて、いけにえとしてささげることまでしました。{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}がイスラエルの人々の前から追い出された国々の人たちの、ひどく汚らわしい習わしをまねたのです。

uk.L: І ходив він дорогою царів Ізраїлю, і навіть свого сина провів через вогонь, за гидотами народів, яких {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}} вигнав перед {{gender:нащадками Ізраїля|синами Ізраїля}}.
uk.B: Він ходив дорогою царів Ізраїлю. Він навіть провів свого сина через вогонь за гидкими звичаями народів, яких {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}} вигнав перед ізраїльтянами.
uk.R: Він жив так, як жили царі Ізраїлю. Він навіть спалив власного сина у вогні як жертву. Він переймав огидні звичаї народів, яких {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}} вигнав з краю перед ізраїльтянами.

decisions.choice: walked in the way of the kings of Israel: followed the northern kings in their worship
decisions.reason: To walk in someone's way is to live as they did. The kings of Israel worshiped at Jeroboam's shrines and, under Ahab, served Baal. Kings says the same of only two earlier kings of Judah, Jehoram and Ahaziah, who were related to Ahab by marriage (8:18, 27).

decisions.choice: made his son pass through the fire: burned his son as an offering
decisions.reason: The phrase names the rite of offering a child by fire to a god. 2 Chronicles 28:3 says of Ahaz that he "burned his sons in the fire", and Jeremiah 7:31 speaks of burning sons and daughters in the fire. Some have thought the phrase could mean a rite of passing a child through fire to dedicate it without killing it, but these passages point to a burnt sacrifice. Ahaz's grandson Manasseh did the same (21:6), and the northern kingdom too (17:17).

decisions.choice: the abominations of the nations: the practices Deuteronomy forbids
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 18:9-10 warns Israel not to learn "the abominations of those nations" and forbids first of all anyone "who makes his son or his daughter pass through the fire" (also Deuteronomy 12:31). Ahaz does what the law named first among those abominations.

decisions.choice: the nations whom Yahweh drove out: the peoples Israel replaced
decisions.reason: Yahweh drove out the peoples of Canaan because of such practices (Deuteronomy 18:12). The king of Judah now takes up the very ways for which those nations lost the land, as was said of Judah under Rehoboam (1 Kings 14:24).

decisions.choice: burned his own son in the fire as a sacrifice
decisions.reason: Readable says what "pass through the fire" meant (m2), as it does at Deuteronomy 18:10. Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew phrase.

decisions.choice: abominations (Literal); detestable practices (Balanced); disgusting practices (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word names what Yahweh finds loathsome. The wording follows 1 Kings 14:24.

decisions.choice: "abominaciones" (L); "prácticas detestables" (B); "prácticas repugnantes" (R)
decisions.reason: One word per level for what Yahweh finds loathsome, following the English levels; Literal keeps "abominaciones", as the published Spanish Literal does elsewhere.

decisions.choice: "quemó a su propio hijo en el fuego como sacrificio"
alternatives: hizo pasar a su hijo por el fuego
decisions.reason: Readable says what "pass through the fire" meant (m2), as the English does; Literal and Balanced keep the phrase.

decisions.choice: "abominations" (L); "pratiques abominables" (B); "pratiques dégoûtantes" (R)
decisions.reason: Each level follows the English choice for the detestable practices of the nations; Readable says plainly that the boy was burned as a sacrifice (m2).

decisions.choice: alimchoma mwanawe mwenyewe motoni kuwa dhabihu
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "passing through the fire" was (meaning decision m2), as the English does.

decisions.choice: machukizo (Literal); desturi za kuchukiza (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: "Machukizo" is the noun for abominations; Balanced and Readable name them as practices, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "불 가운데로 지나가게 했다" (L, B); "불에 태워 제물로 바쳤다" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew's veiled phrase; Readable says what it means, as the English Readable does (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: "가증한 일들" (L); "역겨운 관습" (B); "끔찍한 풍습" (R)
decisions.reason: "가증하다" is the familiar church word; Balanced and Readable use everyday words for what God finds detestable.

decisions.choice: thiêu chính con trai mình trong lửa để làm sinh tế (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what "pass through the fire" meant (m2), as the English does; Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew picture.

decisions.choice: fez o seu filho passar pelo fogo (L, B); queimar o seu próprio filho no fogo como sacrifício (R); abominações (L), coisas abomináveis (B, R)
alternatives: fez o seu filho atravessar o fogo
decisions.reason: The rite (m2) and the abominations (m3) take the words of Deuteronomy 18:10 in Portuguese at each level, so that the reader hears the law Ahaz breaks: "fazer ... passar pelo fogo" at Literal and Balanced, and Readable says what it meant, "queimar ... no fogo como sacrifício", as Deuteronomy 18:10 does. "Abominações" (L) and "coisas abomináveis" (B, R) are the words of 1 Kings 14:24.

decisions.choice: os filhos de Israel (L); os israelitas (B, R), with no gender setting
decisions.reason: As the Old Testament terms set it: "filhos" already includes daughters and "israelitas" names the people, so Portuguese has no second wording for the English gender setting to offer.

decisions.choice: the sons of Israel: "{{gender:इस्राएल की सन्तान|इस्राएल के पुत्रों}}" (L); "इस्राएलियों" (B, R), no span; "आग में से पार कराया" (L, B), "बलि करके आग में जला दिया" (R), in the wording of Deuteronomy 18:10
decisions.reason: As the Pentateuch note settles for the sons of Israel; "इस्राएली" already includes everyone. The child sacrifice is worded as in this translation's Deuteronomy 18:10, the law Ahaz breaks.

decisions.choice: провёл через огонь (L, B); сжёг ... в огне как жертву (R)
decisions.reason: As in Deuteronomy 18:10 in this translation, Literal and Balanced keep "провести через огонь", and Readable says what it means (m2), as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: мерзости (L); мерзкие обычаи (B); отвратительные обычаи (R)
decisions.reason: The wording follows Deuteronomy 18:9 in this translation: the noun at Literal, the practices named at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: to'evot "忌むべき行い / 習わし" (L, B), "ひどく汚らわしい習わし" (R) as DEU; "made his son pass through the fire" kept as "火の中を通らせた" (L, B), explained in R; bene yisra'el unspanned
decisions.reason: Terms as Deuteronomy and 1 Kings; Japanese "子ら" / "人々" need no gender span.

decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew phrase, as the English does; Readable says plainly that the child was sacrificed, as the English Readable does.

ru.R: Он приносил жертвы и сжигал благовония в святилищах на холмах, на вершинах холмов и под каждым большим зелёным деревом.

decisions.choice: made smoke: burned incense or offerings
decisions.reason: The verb means to make something go up in smoke, either incense or parts of an offering. Beside "sacrificed" it describes the worship at the shrines, as at 1 Kings 22:44.

decisions.choice: on the hills and under every leafy tree: the places where the nations worshiped
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 12:2 orders Israel to destroy the places where the nations served their gods "on the high mountains and on the hills and under every leafy tree". Judah built such places under Rehoboam (1 Kings 14:23), and the phrase is used again of Israel's worship (17:10).

decisions.choice: he sacrificed: the king himself, not only the people
decisions.reason: Under the good kings before him "the people" still sacrificed at the high places (15:4, 35). Now the king takes part himself.

decisions.choice: high places (Literal, Balanced); hilltop shrines (Readable); leafy tree
decisions.reason: The wording kept for these words in these books, as at 1 Kings 14:23.

decisions.choice: "los lugares altos" (L, B); "los santuarios sobre las colinas" (R); "árbol frondoso"
decisions.reason: The terms note's wording for the high places; "frondoso" for the leafy tree at every level. Readable says "cerros" for the hills so as not to repeat "colinas".

decisions.choice: imparfait "offrait ... brûlait"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew describes a practice of the king's reign, so French uses the imparfait of repeated action at every level.

decisions.choice: os altos (L, B); os santuários no alto dos morros (R); árvore verdejante (L), frondosa (B, R)
decisions.reason: The wording 1 Kings 14:23 and Deuteronomy 12:2 give these words in Portuguese (m2), level by level, and that 12:4 keeps for the high places in this book.

decisions.choice: под всяким зелёным деревом (L); под каждым ветвистым деревом (B); под каждым большим зелёным деревом (R)
decisions.reason: The phrase keeps the wording of Deuteronomy 12:2 in this translation at Literal and Balanced; Readable adds "большим", as the English adds "large".

decisions.choice: the same attack told in Isaiah 7:1
decisions.reason: Isaiah 7:1 opens with nearly the same words. The differences are small: Isaiah adds "against it" after "for battle", leaves out "they besieged Ahaz", and has "he was not able to fight against it" where Kings has the plural, "they were not able to fight". The wording here follows the translation of Isaiah 7:1 where the Hebrew is the same. Isaiah 7:2-9 tells how the prophet urged Ahaz to stay calm and trust Yahweh during this attack.

decisions.choice: Rezin and Pekah: an alliance against Judah
decisions.reason: Rezin ruled Aram from Damascus and Pekah ruled Israel from Samaria. In the 730s BC, as Assyria pressed west, they marched on Jerusalem; Isaiah 7:6 says they planned to put a king of their own choosing, "the son of Tabeel", on Judah's throne. 2 Chronicles 28:5-8 tells of heavy losses Judah suffered in this war.

decisions.choice: they besieged Ahaz: they shut him up in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: To besiege a king is to surround the city he is in. The king, not only the city, was the target of the attack.

decisions.choice: not able to fight: not able to win the battle
decisions.reason: "Fight" here means to fight the battle through to the end, that is, to take the city. Isaiah 7:1 uses the same verb in this sense.

decisions.choice: take the city / capture it
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "fight" means here (m4), as Isaiah 7:1 does. Readable says "King Rezin" and "King Pekah" and "who ruled Israel", as Isaiah 7:1 does; it leaves out "northern kingdom" there, since Kings uses "Israel" for that kingdom throughout.

decisions.choice: "Rezín"
decisions.reason: The usual Spanish form of Rezin, kept the same through these books.

decisions.choice: Rezim, rei de Arã (L) / rei dos arameus (B, R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the king (m2) takes the nasal ending Portuguese writes for a final "-n", "Rezim", as "Rimom" (5:18) and "Hebrom" do; his title is "rei de Arã" at Literal and "rei dos arameus" at Balanced and Readable, as 5:1, 8:28 and 12:18 have it for this book.

en.L: At that time Rezin king of Aram restored Elath to Aram, and he drove the Judeans out of Elath; and Edomites came [to] Elath, and they have lived there to this day.
en.B: At that time Rezin king of Aram recovered Elath for Aram and drove the people of Judah out of Elath. Edomites came to Elath, and they have lived there to this day.

decisions.choice: Edomites: the reading of the Hebrew tradition; "Aram" kept earlier in the verse
alternatives: the king of Edom recovered Elath for Edom
Arameans came to Elath (the written text)
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew text reads "Arameans" at the end of the verse; the tradition of reading it aloud reads "Edomites", which is followed here. In Hebrew the names Aram and Edom differ by only one letter, and two letters that look much alike. Elath lay at the head of the gulf of the Red Sea, far from Aram and next to Edom, and it had been taken from Edom (14:7, 22). For this reason many think the verse first said that the king of Edom recovered Elath "for Edom", and that "Rezin king of Aram" and "Aram" came in through copying. Every level keeps the Hebrew "Rezin king of Aram ... for Aram"; reviewers should check the evidence.

decisions.choice: Elath: Judah's port on the Red Sea
decisions.reason: Elath stood at the head of the Gulf of Aqaba, near Ezion-geber where Solomon kept his ships (1 Kings 9:26). Azariah of Judah had rebuilt it and restored it to Judah (14:22). "Restored" here takes up that word: Elath now changes hands again. Losing it cut Judah off from the trade of the Red Sea.

decisions.choice: the Judeans: the people of Judah
decisions.reason: This is the first time the word for "Judeans", later "Jews", appears in the Hebrew Bible. Here it means the people of the kingdom of Judah who lived in Elath.

decisions.choice: to this day: the writer's own time
decisions.reason: As at 2:22, "to this day" means up to the time when the account was written: Elath was still in Edomite hands then.

decisions.choice: the people of Judah
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "the people of Judah" so that readers do not take the word in its later sense of the Jewish people as a whole. Literal keeps "Judeans".

decisions.choice: "la gente de Judá"
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "la gente de Judá" so the word is not taken in its later sense, as the English does; Literal keeps "los judíos".

decisions.choice: Elothi; Wayuda
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew's second spelling of the town, Eloth, and its word for the people of Judah; Balanced and Readable use one spelling and say "watu wa Yuda".

decisions.choice: Elate; os judaítas (L); o povo de Judá (B, R)
decisions.reason: The port (m2) takes the final "-e" Portuguese adds after a consonant, "Elate". The people (m3) are "judaítas" at Literal, the Portuguese word for the people of the kingdom of Judah, and "o povo de Judá" at Balanced and Readable, as the English; "judeus" would bring in the later sense of the Jewish people as a whole.

decisions.choice: the Judeans: "አይሁድ" (Literal); "የይሁዳ ሰዎች" (Balanced, Readable); Eloth "ኤሎት" (Literal), "ኤላት" (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew's word and its second spelling of the town; the other levels say who they were and use one spelling, so the reader does not take the Judeans for the Jews of the New Testament or Eloth for a second place.

decisions.choice: "यहूदियों" (L); "यहूदा के लोग" (B, R); "एलोत" kept at Literal where the Hebrew spells the town so
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is the gentilic of Judah; Literal keeps the one word, while Balanced and Readable say "the people of Judah", as the English does, so it is not read as the later Jewish people at large.

decisions.choice: иудеи
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is "the Judeans", the people of Judah (m3); Russian "иудеи" names them at every level, the first time the word is used for the people of the kingdom of Judah.

decisions.choice: Literal keeps the Hebrew's second spelling "エロト" (as 1KI 9:26); Balanced and Readable say "エラト" for both, as the English does
decisions.reason: The Hebrew writes the town both ways in one verse; only Literal shows it.

records.literal_gloss: And sent Ahaz messengers to Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria, saying, your servant and your son [am] I; come up and save me from [the] palm of [the] king of Aram and from [the] palm of [the] king of Israel, the [ones] rising up against me.

en.L: And Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria, saying, "Your servant and your son [am] I. Come up and save me from the hand of the king of Aram and from the hand of the king of Israel, who are rising up against me."
en.B: Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria with this message: "I am your servant and your son. Come up and rescue me from the power of the king of Aram and the king of Israel, who are attacking me."
en.R: Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath-pileser, the king of Assyria, with this message: "I am your servant and your son. Come and save me from the king of Aram and the king of Israel. They are attacking me."

es.L: Y Acaz envió mensajeros a Tiglat-piléser, rey de Asiria, diciendo: «Tu siervo y tu hijo [soy] yo; sube y sálvame de la palma del rey de Aram y de la palma del rey de Israel, que se levantan contra mí».
es.B: Acaz envió mensajeros a Tiglat-piléser, rey de Asiria, con este mensaje: «Yo soy tu siervo y tu hijo. Sube y líbrame del poder del rey de Aram y del rey de Israel, que me atacan».
es.R: Acaz envió mensajeros a Tiglat-piléser, el rey de Asiria, con este mensaje: «Yo soy tu siervo y tu hijo. Ven a salvarme del rey de Aram y del rey de Israel. Me están atacando».

fr.L: Et Achaz envoya des messagers à Tiglath-Piléser, roi d’Assyrie, pour dire : « Ton serviteur et ton fils, [c’est] moi. Monte et sauve-moi de la main du roi d’Aram et de la main du roi d’Israël, qui se dressent contre moi. »
fr.B: Achaz envoya des messagers à Tiglath-Piléser, roi d’Assyrie, avec ce message : « Je suis ton serviteur et ton fils. Monte me délivrer du pouvoir du roi d’Aram et du roi d’Israël, qui m’attaquent. »
fr.R: Achaz a envoyé des messagers à Tiglath-Piléser, le roi d’Assyrie, avec ce message : « Je suis ton serviteur et ton fils. Viens me sauver du roi d’Aram et du roi d’Israël. Ils m’attaquent. »

decisions.choice: Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria
decisions.reason: Tiglath-pileser III ruled Assyria from 745 to 727 BC and pushed its empire west to the Mediterranean. He is also called Pul (15:19), and he had already taken towns of northern Israel in Pekah's reign (15:29).

decisions.choice: your servant and your son: the words of a vassal to his overlord
decisions.reason: A king who calls himself another king's servant and son places himself under him as a subject king, owing loyalty and tribute. Ahaz offers Judah's submission to Assyria in return for help.

decisions.choice: son ... save me: help sought from Assyria rather than from Yahweh
decisions.reason: Yahweh had promised that David's heir would be a son to him (2 Samuel 7:14), and through Isaiah he told Ahaz not to fear these two kings but to trust him (Isaiah 7:4, 9). Ahaz instead calls himself the Assyrian king's son and asks him to save.

decisions.choice: from the palm of: from the power of
decisions.reason: The hand or palm stands for power or control. Rising up against someone means attacking him.

decisions.choice: your servant at every level
decisions.reason: As in other polite or submissive self-references, "your servant" stands at every level. Here it is the formal language of a subject king (m2), and "slave" would suggest a household slave rather than a vassal.

decisions.choice: save me from the king of Aram and the king of Israel. They are attacking me.
decisions.reason: Readable leaves out the picture of the hand (m4) and puts "rising up against me" in a sentence of its own.

decisions.choice: "tu siervo" at every level; "tú" to the king of Assyria
decisions.reason: "Tu siervo" stands at every level, as the Samuel terms note sets for a subject speaking to a king; Spanish uses "tú" to kings and never "usted", and the submission is carried by "siervo" and "hijo" (m2).

decisions.choice: "ton serviteur" at every level
decisions.reason: A vassal's words to his overlord (m2); as the English and the Samuel note for "your servant" in speech to a king, "serviteur" serves at every level, Literal included.

decisions.choice: mtumishi wako at every level
decisions.reason: A vassal speaking to his overlord, in the wording used for "your servant" to a king in Samuel.

decisions.choice: tôi ... đầy tớ của vua và con của vua
decisions.reason: Ahaz writes as a vassal: "đầy tớ của vua" stands at every level, as the English keeps "your servant", and he says "tôi" rather than the court's "bệ hạ", since he is himself a king.

decisions.choice: Ahaz writes to the king of Assyria in the formal style (합쇼체), calling himself "저" and "임금님의 종"
decisions.reason: "Your servant and your son" are the words of a vassal to his overlord (meaning decision m2); Korean shows the submission by the speech level as well as by the words.

decisions.choice: Tiglate-Pileser, rei da Assíria; o seu servo (every level), addressed as "o senhor"
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the Assyrian king (m1) is written as Portuguese writes the sounds of his name, "Tiglate-Pileser", with the final "-e" it adds after a consonant. Ahaz speaks as a subject king to his overlord (m2): the courtly "o seu servo" at every level, as the English keeps "your servant", and the forms that go with "o senhor"; "escravo" would suggest a household slave.

decisions.choice: Ahaz to the king of Assyria: "እርስዎ", "ባሪያዎ" (Literal) / "አገልጋይዎ" (Balanced, Readable), "ልጅዎ"
decisions.reason: Ahaz speaks as a vassal to his overlord, so he uses the respectful address of a subject to a king, as the terms list sets it.

decisions.choice: "मैं आपका दास और आपका पुत्र हूँ": Ahaz says "आप" to the king of Assyria
decisions.reason: The words are those of a vassal to his overlord, and Hindi carries the submission with "आप" and "दास" at every level.

decisions.choice: твой раб (every level)
decisions.reason: A vassal speaks to his overlord (m2); as the Pentateuch note settles, the Hebrew word is "раб" at every level, and here it marks submission, not service.

decisions.choice: Ahaz to the Assyrian king です・ます, with "あなたのしもべ、あなたの子" at every level
decisions.reason: The words of a vassal to his overlord (m2); the humble "しもべ" as for "your servant" elsewhere.

decisions.choice: "твій раб" at every level for the vassalʼs "your servant"
decisions.reason: A subject kingʼs self-description to his overlord; the terms note keeps "раб" for ʿeved, and here the submission is the point.

pt.L: E Acaz tomou a prata e o ouro que se achavam na casa {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} e nos tesouros da casa do rei, e [os] enviou ao rei da Assíria [como] suborno.

ru.R: Ахаз взял серебро и золото, которое было в храме {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Яхве}} и в сокровищницах царского дворца. Всё это он послал царю Ассирии, чтобы подкупить его.

uk.R: Ахаз забрав срібло й золото, що було в храмі {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Ягве}} і в скарбницях царського палацу. Він послав його цареві Ассирії як хабар.

decisions.choice: bribe: a payment to buy someone's action
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for a bribe that bends a judge (Exodus 23:8; Deuteronomy 16:19), not a friendly gift. Asa used the same word when he paid Ben-hadad to break a treaty (1 Kings 15:19). Ahaz buys Assyria's help with the temple's wealth.

decisions.choice: emptying the treasuries: as Asa and Jehoash had done
decisions.reason: Asa sent the treasures of the temple and the palace to Damascus to buy help against Israel (1 Kings 15:18), and Jehoash of Judah paid off Hazael with them (12:19). Now Ahaz pays Assyria to strike Damascus.

decisions.choice: found: what was there
decisions.reason: "Found" means whatever was on hand at the time in the temple and the royal treasuries.

decisions.choice: the temple of the LORD; treasure rooms of the royal palace
decisions.reason: Readable says "temple" for the house of Yahweh and "royal palace" for the house of the king, as these books do.

decisions.choice: "la casa del SEÑOR" (L, B); "el templo del SEÑOR" (R); "palacio" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the terms note sets for the house of the LORD; Balanced and Readable name the king's house as the palace.

decisions.choice: "présent corrupteur" (L); "pour l'acheter" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word is a payment that buys someone's action (m1); "pot-de-vin" sounds too modern and petty for a tribute between kings, so Balanced and Readable say what the gift was for.

decisions.choice: suborno
decisions.reason: "Suborno" is the word 1 Kings 15:19 gives Asa's payment in Portuguese (m1, m2): a payment to buy someone's action, not a friendly gift.

decisions.choice: "ጉቦ" for the bribe
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is the one for a bribe, not a gift of homage; "ጉቦ" keeps its edge.

decisions.choice: подарок (L); подкуп (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is a gift paid to buy someone's action (m1); Literal says "подарок", the plain word, and Balanced and Readable name it for what it is, "подкуп".

decisions.choice: shochad "贈り物" at every level, as 1KI 15:19
decisions.reason: The English says bribe; 1 Kings settled "贈り物" for this payment between kings, and the footnote (m1) gives the sense of a payment to buy help.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע אֵלָיו֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר וַיַּעַל֩ מֶ֨לֶךְ אַשּׁ֤וּר אֶל־דַּמֶּ֨שֶׂק֙ וַֽיִּתְפְּשֶׂ֔הָ וַיַּגְלֶ֖הָ קִ֑ירָה וְאֶת־רְצִ֖ין הֵמִֽית׃

records.literal_gloss: And listened to him [the] king of Assyria, and went up [the] king of Assyria to Damascus and seized it, and he exiled it [to] Kir, and Rezin he put to death.

en.L: And the king of Assyria listened to him, and the king of Assyria went up against Damascus and seized it, and he carried it [into exile to] Kir, and he put Rezin to death.
en.B: The king of Assyria agreed to his request. He marched up against Damascus and captured it. He took its people into exile to Kir and put Rezin to death.
en.R: The king of Assyria agreed to help Ahaz. He attacked Damascus and captured it. He forced its people to move to Kir as captives, and he killed Rezin.

es.L: Y el rey de Asiria lo escuchó, y subió el rey de Asiria contra Damasco y la tomó, y la llevó cautiva [a] Quir, y dio muerte a Rezín.
es.B: El rey de Asiria accedió a su petición. Subió contra Damasco y la conquistó. Llevó cautivos a sus habitantes a Quir y dio muerte a Rezín.
es.R: El rey de Asiria aceptó ayudar a Acaz. Atacó Damasco y la conquistó. Obligó a sus habitantes a irse a Quir como prisioneros, y mató a Rezín.

fr.L: Et le roi d’Assyrie l’écouta, et le roi d’Assyrie monta contre Damas et la prit, et il la déporta [à] Qir, et il fit mourir Retsin.
fr.B: Le roi d’Assyrie accéda à sa demande. Il monta contre Damas et s’en empara. Il en déporta les habitants à Qir et fit mourir Retsin.
fr.R: Le roi d’Assyrie a accepté d’aider Achaz. Il a attaqué Damas et l’a prise. Il a obligé ses habitants à partir comme prisonniers à Qir, et il a tué Retsin.

sw.L: Naye mfalme wa Ashuru akamsikiliza, na mfalme wa Ashuru akapanda juu ya Dameski, akaitwaa, akaihamisha [mpaka] Kiri, naye akamwua Resini.
sw.B: Mfalme wa Ashuru alikubali ombi lake. Akapanda kuishambulia Dameski, akaiteka. Akawachukua watu wake uhamishoni mpaka Kiri, akamwua Resini.
sw.R: Mfalme wa Ashuru alikubali kumsaidia Ahazi. Aliishambulia Dameski, akaiteka. Aliwalazimisha watu wake kuhamia Kiri wakiwa mateka, naye akamwua Resini.

vi.L: Vua A-si-ri nghe lời ông; vua A-si-ri đi lên đánh Đa-mách và chiếm lấy, bắt [dân] nó lưu đày [đến] Ki-rơ, và giết Rê-xin.
vi.B: Vua A-si-ri chấp thuận lời yêu cầu của A-cha. Vua ấy tiến đánh Đa-mách và chiếm được thành, bắt dân thành lưu đày đến Ki-rơ và xử tử Rê-xin.
vi.R: Vua A-si-ri đồng ý giúp A-cha. Vua ấy tấn công Đa-mách và chiếm được thành. Vua ấy bắt dân thành phải dời đến Ki-rơ làm tù binh, và giết Rê-xin.

ko.L: 그리고 앗시리아 왕이 그의 말을 들었다. 그리고 앗시리아 왕이 다메섹으로 올라가 그곳을 점령하고, 그곳을 기르로 사로잡아 갔으며, 르신을 죽였다.
ko.B: 앗시리아 왕은 그의 청을 들어주었다. 그는 다메섹으로 올라가 그 성을 점령하고, 그 백성을 기르로 사로잡아 갔으며, 르신을 죽였다.
ko.R: 앗시리아 왕은 아하스를 도와주기로 했다. 그는 다메섹을 공격하여 빼앗았다. 그는 그곳 백성을 포로로 잡아 기르로 옮겨 살게 했고, 르신을 죽였다.

pt.L: E o rei da Assíria o ouviu, e o rei da Assíria subiu contra Damasco e a tomou, e a levou [para o exílio em] Quir, e matou Rezim.
pt.B: O rei da Assíria atendeu ao pedido dele. Marchou contra Damasco e a conquistou. Levou os seus habitantes para o exílio em Quir e matou Rezim.
pt.R: O rei da Assíria concordou em ajudar Acaz. Ele atacou Damasco e a conquistou. Obrigou os moradores da cidade a ir como prisioneiros para Quir, e matou Rezim.

am.L: የአሦርም ንጉሥ ሰማው፤ የአሦርም ንጉሥ ወደ ደማስቆ ወጥቶ ያዛት፤ ወደ ቂርም አፈለሳት፤ ረአሶንንም ገደለ።
am.B: የአሦር ንጉሥ ልመናውን ተቀበለ። በደማስቆ ላይ ወጥቶ ያዛት። ሕዝቧንም ማርኮ ወደ ቂር ወሰደ፤ ረአሶንንም ገደለ።
am.R: የአሦር ንጉሥ አካዝን ለመርዳት ተስማማ። ደማስቆን ወግቶ ያዛት። ሕዝቧንም ምርኮኞች አድርጎ ወደ ቂር እንዲሄዱ አስገደዳቸው፤ ረአሶንንም ገደለ።

hi.L: और अश्शूर के राजा ने उसकी सुनी, और अश्शूर का राजा दमिश्क पर चढ़ गया और उसे ले लिया, और उसे निर्वासित करके कीर [ले गया], और रसीन को मार डाला।
hi.B: अश्शूर के राजा ने उसकी बात मान ली। उसने दमिश्क पर चढ़ाई करके उसे जीत लिया। वह वहाँ के लोगों को निर्वासित करके कीर ले गया और रसीन को मार डाला।
hi.R: अश्शूर का राजा आहाज़ की सहायता करने को मान गया। उसने दमिश्क पर हमला करके उसे जीत लिया। वह वहाँ के लोगों को बंदी बनाकर कीर ले गया, और उसने रसीन को मार डाला।

ru.L: И послушал его царь Ассирии, и поднялся царь Ассирии на Дамаск, и взял его, и переселил его [жителей в] Кир, а Рецина умертвил.
ru.B: Царь Ассирии согласился на его просьбу. Он выступил против Дамаска и взял его. Жителей он увёл в изгнание в Кир, а Рецина казнил.
ru.R: Царь Ассирии согласился помочь Ахазу. Он напал на Дамаск и захватил его. Жителей Дамаска он угнал в плен в Кир, а Рецина убил.

ja.L: そしてアッシリアの王は彼に聞き従った。そしてアッシリアの王はダマスコに上って行ってそれを捕らえ、それをキルへ捕らえ移し、レツィンを殺した。
ja.B: アッシリアの王はその願いを聞き入れた。彼はダマスコに攻め上ってそこを攻め取り、住民をキルへ捕囚として連れ去り、レツィンを殺した。
ja.R: アッシリアの王は、アハズを助けることにしました。アッシリアの王はダマスコを攻めて、その町を攻め取りました。そして、そこの人々を捕虜にしてキルへ連れて行き、レツィンを殺しました。

uk.L: І вислухав його цар Ассирії, і піднявся цар Ассирії на Дамаск, і захопив його, і переселив його [мешканців до] Кіру, а Рецина вбив.
uk.B: Цар Ассирії погодився на його прохання. Він пішов на Дамаск і захопив його. Його мешканців він переселив до Кіру, а Рецина стратив.
uk.R: Цар Ассирії погодився допомогти Ахазові. Він напав на Дамаск і захопив його. Він вигнав його мешканців у полон до Кіру, а Рецина вбив.

decisions.choice: listened to him: agreed to his request
decisions.reason: To listen to a request is to agree to it and act on it, as at 1 Kings 15:20.

decisions.choice: the fall of Damascus: the end of the kingdom of Aram
decisions.reason: Damascus fell to Assyria in 732 BC. Its king was killed and its land became part of the Assyrian empire. Isaiah had foretold that Damascus would be plundered before the child of the sign could speak (Isaiah 8:4; 7:16).

decisions.choice: Kir: where the Arameans came from
decisions.reason: Amos had foretold that the people of Aram would go into exile to Kir (Amos 1:5), and he names Kir as the place from which Yahweh brought the Arameans (Amos 9:7). They are sent back where their history began. Where Kir lay is not known.

decisions.choice: exiled it: carried off its people
decisions.reason: "It" refers to the city, meaning its people. Assyria moved conquered peoples to distant lands to break their resistance (17:6).

decisions.choice: its people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who was carried off (m4). Readable also says "agreed to help Ahaz" and explains exile as being forced to move as captives.

decisions.choice: "a sus habitantes"
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who was carried off (m4); Literal keeps "la llevó cautiva", with the city as object. "Quir" is the usual Spanish form of Kir.

decisions.choice: Quir
decisions.reason: The place (m3) is written "Quir", as Portuguese writes the sound of a "k" before "i".

decisions.choice: "キル" for Kir
decisions.reason: The usual modern Japanese form.

source.text: וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אָחָ֡ז לִ֠קְרַאת תִּגְלַ֨ת פִּלְאֶ֤סֶר מֶֽלֶךְ־אַשּׁוּר֙ דּוּמֶּ֔שֶׂק וַיַּ֥רְא אֶת־הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּדַמָּ֑שֶׂק וַיִּשְׁלַח֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ אָחָ֜ז אֶל־אוּרִיָּ֣ה הַכֹּהֵ֗ן אֶת־דְּמ֧וּת הַמִּזְבֵּ֛חַ וְאֶת־תַּבְנִית֖וֹ לְכָֽל־מַעֲשֵֽׂהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And went the king Ahaz to meet Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria [at] Damascus, and he saw the altar which [was] in Damascus; and sent the king Ahaz to Uriah the priest [the] likeness of the altar and its pattern, for all its workmanship.

en.L: And King Ahaz went to meet Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria [at] Damascus, and he saw the altar that [was] in Damascus. And King Ahaz sent to Uriah the priest the likeness of the altar and its pattern, for all its workmanship.
en.B: King Ahaz went to meet Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria at Damascus. There he saw the altar that stood in Damascus. Then King Ahaz sent Uriah the priest a model and a design of the altar, with all the details of how it was made.
en.R: King Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglath-pileser, the king of Assyria. While he was there, he saw the altar in Damascus. He sent Uriah the priest a model of the altar and a plan that showed exactly how it was made.

es.L: Y fue el rey Acaz al encuentro de Tiglat-piléser, rey de Asiria, [a] Damasco, y vio el altar que [estaba] en Damasco. Y el rey Acaz envió al sacerdote Urías la imagen del altar y su modelo, conforme a toda su hechura.
es.B: El rey Acaz fue a Damasco al encuentro de Tiglat-piléser, rey de Asiria. Allí vio el altar que había en Damasco. Entonces el rey Acaz le envió al sacerdote Urías una maqueta y un diseño del altar, con todos los detalles de su construcción.
es.R: El rey Acaz fue a Damasco para encontrarse con Tiglat-piléser, el rey de Asiria. Mientras estaba allí, vio el altar de Damasco. Le envió al sacerdote Urías una maqueta del altar y un plano que mostraba exactamente cómo estaba hecho.

fr.L: Et le roi Achaz alla à la rencontre de Tiglath-Piléser, roi d’Assyrie, [à] Damas, et il vit l’autel qui [était] à Damas. Et le roi Achaz envoya au prêtre Urie la forme de l’autel et son modèle, selon toute sa fabrication.
fr.B: Le roi Achaz alla à Damas au-devant de Tiglath-Piléser, roi d’Assyrie. Là, il vit l’autel qui se trouvait à Damas. Alors le roi Achaz envoya au prêtre Urie une maquette et un plan de l’autel, avec tous les détails de sa fabrication.
fr.R: Le roi Achaz est allé à Damas pour rencontrer Tiglath-Piléser, le roi d’Assyrie. Pendant qu’il était là-bas, il a vu l’autel de Damas. Il a envoyé au prêtre Urie une maquette de l’autel et un plan qui montrait exactement comment le construire.

sw.L: Naye mfalme Ahazi akaenda kumlaki Tiglath-pileseri mfalme wa Ashuru [huko] Dameski, akaiona madhabahu iliyokuwa huko Dameski. Naye mfalme Ahazi akampelekea Uria kuhani mfano wa madhabahu hiyo na ramani yake, kwa kazi yake yote.
sw.B: Mfalme Ahazi alikwenda kukutana na Tiglath-pileseri mfalme wa Ashuru huko Dameski. Huko akaiona madhabahu iliyokuwa Dameski. Kisha mfalme Ahazi akampelekea Uria kuhani mfano na ramani ya madhabahu hiyo, pamoja na maelezo yote ya jinsi ilivyotengenezwa.
sw.R: Mfalme Ahazi alikwenda Dameski kukutana na Tiglath-pileseri, mfalme wa Ashuru. Alipokuwa huko, aliiona madhabahu ya Dameski. Akampelekea Uria kuhani mfano wa madhabahu hiyo na ramani iliyoonyesha hasa jinsi ilivyotengenezwa.

vi.L: Vua A-cha đi gặp Tiếc-la-Phi-lê-se vua A-si-ri [tại] Đa-mách, và thấy bàn thờ ở Đa-mách. Vua A-cha gửi cho thầy tế lễ U-ri hình dạng của bàn thờ và kiểu mẫu của nó, theo mọi chi tiết cách làm.
vi.B: Vua A-cha đi đến Đa-mách để gặp Tiếc-la-Phi-lê-se vua A-si-ri. Tại đó vua thấy bàn thờ ở Đa-mách. Vua A-cha liền gửi cho thầy tế lễ U-ri một mô hình và bản vẽ của bàn thờ ấy, với mọi chi tiết về cách làm.
vi.R: Vua A-cha đi đến Đa-mách để gặp Tiếc-la-Phi-lê-se, vua A-si-ri. Khi ở đó, vua thấy bàn thờ tại Đa-mách. Vua gửi cho thầy tế lễ U-ri một mô hình của bàn thờ ấy và một bản vẽ chỉ rõ cách làm.

ko.L: 그리고 아하스 왕이 앗시리아 왕 디글랏빌레셀을 만나러 다메섹에 갔다가, 다메섹에 있는 제단을 보았다. 그리고 아하스 왕이 그 제단의 모양과 그 양식을, 그 모든 만듦새대로 제사장 우리야에게 보냈다.
ko.B: 아하스 왕은 앗시리아 왕 디글랏빌레셀을 만나러 다메섹에 갔다. 거기에서 그는 다메섹에 있는 제단을 보았다. 그러자 아하스 왕은 그 제단의 모형과 설계도를 그 세부 구조까지 모두 그려서 제사장 우리야에게 보냈다.
ko.R: 아하스 왕은 앗시리아 왕 디글랏빌레셀을 만나러 다메섹으로 갔다. 거기에 있는 동안 그는 다메섹에 있는 제단을 보았다. 그는 제사장 우리야에게 그 제단의 모형과, 그것을 어떻게 만드는지 자세히 보여 주는 설계도를 보냈다.

pt.L: E o rei Acaz foi ao encontro de Tiglate-Pileser, rei da Assíria, [em] Damasco, e viu o altar que [estava] em Damasco. E o rei Acaz enviou a Urias, o sacerdote, a semelhança do altar e o seu modelo, conforme toda a sua obra.
pt.B: O rei Acaz foi a Damasco para se encontrar com Tiglate-Pileser, rei da Assíria. Ali viu o altar que havia em Damasco. Então o rei Acaz enviou a Urias, o sacerdote, uma maquete e um modelo do altar, com todos os detalhes de como era feito.
pt.R: O rei Acaz foi a Damasco para se encontrar com Tiglate-Pileser, o rei da Assíria. Enquanto estava lá, viu o altar de Damasco. Ele mandou a Urias, o sacerdote, uma maquete do altar e um desenho que mostrava exatamente como ele era feito.

am.L: ንጉሡ አካዝም የአሦርን ንጉሥ ቴልጌልቴልፌልሶርን ሊገናኘው ወደ ደማስቆ ሄደ፤ በደማስቆም ያለውን መሠዊያ አየ፤ ንጉሡ አካዝም የመሠዊያውን ምሳሌና ንድፉን እንደ አሠራሩ ሁሉ ወደ ካህኑ ወደ ኦርዮ ላከ።
am.B: ንጉሥ አካዝ የአሦርን ንጉሥ ቴልጌልቴልፌልሶርን ሊገናኝ ወደ ደማስቆ ሄደ። በዚያም በደማስቆ የቆመውን መሠዊያ አየ። ከዚያም ንጉሥ አካዝ የመሠዊያውን ቅርጽና ንድፍ፣ አሠራሩንም በዝርዝር ለካህኑ ለኦርዮ ላከ።

hi.L: और राजा आहाज़ अश्शूर के राजा तिग्लत-पिलेसेर से भेंट करने दमिश्क गया, और उसने वह वेदी देखी जो दमिश्क में [थी]; और राजा आहाज़ ने ऊरिय्याह याजक के पास वेदी का नमूना और उसकी रूपरेखा, उसकी सारी बनावट के अनुसार, भेजी।
hi.B: राजा आहाज़ अश्शूर के राजा तिग्लत-पिलेसेर से भेंट करने दमिश्क गया। वहाँ उसने वह वेदी देखी जो दमिश्क में थी। तब राजा आहाज़ ने ऊरिय्याह याजक के पास उस वेदी का नमूना और उसकी रूपरेखा भेजी, जिसमें उसकी बनावट की सारी बातें थीं।
hi.R: राजा आहाज़ अश्शूर के राजा तिग्लत-पिलेसेर से मिलने दमिश्क गया। वहाँ रहते हुए उसने दमिश्क की वेदी देखी। उसने ऊरिय्याह याजक के पास उस वेदी का एक नमूना और एक नक़्शा भेजा, जिसमें ठीक-ठीक दिखाया गया था कि वह कैसे बनी है।

ru.L: И пошёл царь Ахаз навстречу Тиглатпаласару, царю Ассирии, [в] Дамаск, и увидел жертвенник, который [был] в Дамаске. И послал царь Ахаз Урии, священнику, подобие жертвенника и его образец, по всей его работе.
ru.B: Царь Ахаз отправился в Дамаск, чтобы встретиться с Тиглатпаласаром, царём Ассирии. Там он увидел жертвенник, стоявший в Дамаске. Тогда царь Ахаз послал священнику Урии модель жертвенника и его чертёж со всеми подробностями его устройства.
ru.R: Царь Ахаз поехал в Дамаск, чтобы встретиться с Тиглатпаласаром, царём Ассирии. Там он увидел жертвенник. Он послал священнику Урии модель этого жертвенника и чертёж, на котором было точно показано, как он сделан.

ja.L: そしてアハズ王はアッシリアの王ティグラト・ピレセルに会うためにダマスコへ行き、ダマスコにある祭壇を見た。そしてアハズ王は祭司ウリヤに、その祭壇の模型と、その造りのすべてにわたる設計図を送った。
ja.B: アハズ王は、アッシリアの王ティグラト・ピレセルに会うためにダマスコへ行った。そこで、ダマスコにある祭壇を見た。そこでアハズ王は祭司ウリヤに、その祭壇の模型と、造り方を細かく示した設計図を送った。
ja.R: アハズ王は、アッシリアの王ティグラト・ピレセルに会うために、ダマスコへ行きました。そこにいる間に、アハズはダマスコにある祭壇を見ました。そこで、祭司ウリヤに、その祭壇の模型と、どのように造るかを細かく示した設計図を送りました。

uk.L: І пішов цар Ахаз назустріч Тіглат-Пілесерові, цареві Ассирії, [до] Дамаску, і побачив жертовник, що [був] у Дамаску. І послав цар Ахаз Урії, священникові, подобу жертовника і його взірець, за всією його роботою.
uk.B: Цар Ахаз пішов до Дамаску назустріч Тіглат-Пілесерові, цареві Ассирії. Там він побачив жертовник, що стояв у Дамаску. Тоді цар Ахаз послав священникові Урії модель і креслення жертовника з усіма подробицями його виготовлення.
uk.R: Цар Ахаз пішов до Дамаску зустрітися з Тіглат-Пілесером, царем Ассирії. Там він побачив жертовник. Він послав священникові Урії модель жертовника і креслення, на якому було точно показано, як його зроблено.

decisions.choice: went to meet the king of Assyria: a subject king presenting himself
decisions.reason: Ahaz goes to the conquered city of Damascus to appear before his new overlord, as subject kings were required to do.

decisions.choice: the altar in Damascus: a foreign altar
decisions.reason: The text does not say whose altar it was, an Aramean one or one the Assyrians set up, or to which god it belonged. What matters to the writer is that the new altar of Yahweh's temple is copied from it.

decisions.choice: likeness and pattern: a design from Damascus instead of from Yahweh
decisions.reason: The word "pattern" is the one used for the pattern of the tabernacle and its furnishings that Yahweh showed Moses (Exodus 25:9, 40), and for the plan of the temple David gave Solomon (1 Chronicles 28:11-19). Here the pattern for the altar comes from a foreign city.

decisions.choice: Uriah the priest: the chief priest at the temple
decisions.reason: Uriah appears to be the leading priest in Jerusalem. Isaiah names "Uriah the priest" as a reliable witness (Isaiah 8:2), most likely the same man.

decisions.choice: a model ... its design / a plan; with all the details of how it was made
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "model" for "likeness" and "design" or "plan" for "pattern", and turn "for all its workmanship" into a plain phrase. Readable adds "While he was there" to link the two events.

decisions.choice: "una maqueta y un diseño" (B); "una maqueta ... y un plano" (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "likeness" and "pattern" were, a model and a design, as the English does; Literal keeps "imagen" and "modelo". "Urías" is the usual Spanish form.

decisions.choice: Urias, o sacerdote; a semelhança ... o seu modelo (L); uma maquete e um modelo (B); uma maquete ... e um desenho (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole passage (verses 10-16): the priest (m4) is "Urias, o sacerdote" at every level, as the English keeps "Uriah the priest". The "pattern" (m3) is "modelo" at Literal and Balanced, the word Exodus 25:9 gives the pattern of the tabernacle in Portuguese, so that the reader can hear that the design now comes from Damascus; "semelhança" at Literal is the word of Genesis 1:26. Balanced and Readable say "maquete" for the likeness, as the English says "model".

decisions.choice: Uriah the priest: "ኦርዮ"
decisions.reason: The same Hebrew name as Uriah the Hittite (2 Samuel 11), so the same Amharic form.

decisions.choice: "祭司ウリヤ", the same form as Uriah the Hittite "ヘト人ウリヤ"; demut "模型", tavnit "設計図"
decisions.reason: One Hebrew name, one Japanese form; the title tells the men apart.

decisions.choice: "Урія" for the priest; "Кір" for the place of exile; "Єзекія" in 16:20
decisions.reason: "Урія" as for Uriah the Hittite in 1 Kings 15:5; "Єзекія" is the terms noteʼs form.

records.literal_gloss: And built Uriah the priest the altar according to all that had sent the king Ahaz from Damascus; so did Uriah the priest until [the] coming of the king Ahaz from Damascus.

en.L: And Uriah the priest built the altar according to all that King Ahaz had sent from Damascus; so Uriah the priest did, until King Ahaz came from Damascus.
en.B: Uriah the priest built the altar following everything King Ahaz had sent from Damascus. He had it finished by the time King Ahaz came back from Damascus.
en.R: Uriah the priest built the altar exactly like the model and plan King Ahaz had sent from Damascus. He finished it before King Ahaz came home.

es.L: Y el sacerdote Urías edificó el altar conforme a todo lo que el rey Acaz había enviado de Damasco; así lo hizo el sacerdote Urías, hasta que vino el rey Acaz de Damasco.
es.B: El sacerdote Urías construyó el altar siguiendo todo lo que el rey Acaz le había enviado de Damasco. Lo tuvo terminado para cuando el rey Acaz volvió de Damasco.
es.R: El sacerdote Urías construyó el altar exactamente igual que la maqueta y el plano que el rey Acaz le había enviado de Damasco. Lo terminó antes de que el rey Acaz regresara.

fr.L: Et le prêtre Urie bâtit l’autel selon tout ce que le roi Achaz avait envoyé de Damas ; ainsi fit le prêtre Urie, jusqu’à ce que le roi Achaz revienne de Damas.
fr.B: Le prêtre Urie construisit l’autel en suivant tout ce que le roi Achaz avait envoyé de Damas. Il l’eut achevé avant que le roi Achaz revienne de Damas.
fr.R: Le prêtre Urie a construit l’autel exactement d’après la maquette et le plan que le roi Achaz avait envoyés de Damas. Il l’a terminé avant le retour du roi.

sw.L: Naye Uria kuhani akaijenga madhabahu sawasawa na yote aliyoyatuma mfalme Ahazi kutoka Dameski; ndivyo alivyofanya Uria kuhani, hata kuja kwa mfalme Ahazi kutoka Dameski.
sw.B: Uria kuhani aliijenga madhabahu akifuata kila kitu mfalme Ahazi alichokuwa amekituma kutoka Dameski. Alikuwa ameimaliza kabla mfalme Ahazi hajarudi kutoka Dameski.
sw.R: Uria kuhani aliijenga madhabahu sawasawa kabisa na mfano na ramani ambayo mfalme Ahazi alikuwa ametuma kutoka Dameski. Aliimaliza kabla mfalme Ahazi hajarudi nyumbani.

pt.L: E Urias, o sacerdote, edificou o altar conforme tudo o que o rei Acaz tinha enviado de Damasco; assim fez Urias, o sacerdote, até que o rei Acaz veio de Damasco.
pt.B: Urias, o sacerdote, construiu o altar seguindo tudo o que o rei Acaz tinha enviado de Damasco. Ele o deixou pronto antes que o rei Acaz voltasse de Damasco.
pt.R: Urias, o sacerdote, construiu o altar exatamente como a maquete e o desenho que o rei Acaz tinha mandado de Damasco. Ele terminou o altar antes que o rei Acaz voltasse para casa.

hi.L: और ऊरिय्याह याजक ने उस सब के अनुसार वेदी बनाई जो राजा आहाज़ ने दमिश्क से भेजा था; ऊरिय्याह याजक ने राजा आहाज़ के दमिश्क से आने तक ऐसा ही किया।
hi.B: ऊरिय्याह याजक ने वेदी को ठीक वैसा ही बनाया जैसा राजा आहाज़ ने दमिश्क से भेजा था। राजा आहाज़ के दमिश्क से लौटने तक उसने उसे बनाकर तैयार कर दिया।
hi.R: ऊरिय्याह याजक ने वेदी ठीक उसी नमूने और नक़्शे के अनुसार बनाई जो राजा आहाज़ ने दमिश्क से भेजा था। राजा आहाज़ के घर लौटने से पहले ही उसने उसे बना दिया।

ru.L: И построил Урия, священник, жертвенник по всему, что прислал царь Ахаз из Дамаска; так сделал Урия, священник, до прихода царя Ахаза из Дамаска.
ru.B: Священник Урия построил жертвенник во всём по тому, что прислал царь Ахаз из Дамаска. Он закончил его к тому времени, когда царь Ахаз вернулся из Дамаска.
ru.R: Священник Урия построил жертвенник точно по модели и чертежу, которые царь Ахаз прислал из Дамаска. Он закончил его ещё до возвращения царя Ахаза.

ja.L: そして祭司ウリヤは、アハズ王がダマスコから送ったすべてのとおりに祭壇を築いた。祭司ウリヤは、アハズ王がダマスコから帰って来るまでに、そのようにした。
ja.B: 祭司ウリヤは、アハズ王がダマスコから送ったものにすべて従って祭壇を築き、アハズ王がダマスコから帰って来るまでに仕上げた。
ja.R: 祭司ウリヤは、アハズ王がダマスコから送った模型と設計図のとおりに、祭壇を築きました。そして、アハズ王が帰って来る前に、それを仕上げました。

uk.L: І збудував Урія, священник, жертовник за всім, що прислав цар Ахаз з Дамаску; так зробив Урія, священник, поки не прийшов цар Ахаз з Дамаску.
uk.B: Священник Урія збудував жертовник за всім, що прислав цар Ахаз з Дамаску. Він закінчив його до того часу, як цар Ахаз повернувся з Дамаску.
uk.R: Священник Урія збудував жертовник точно за моделлю і кресленням, які прислав цар Ахаз з Дамаску. Він закінчив його ще до того, як цар Ахаз повернувся додому.

decisions.choice: so Uriah did until the king came: the work was done before the king returned
decisions.reason: The second half of the verse repeats that Uriah followed the king's instructions, and adds that he did so in the time before Ahaz came back. The altar was ready when he arrived (verse 12).

decisions.choice: according to all that the king had sent: the priest follows the king's design
decisions.reason: The words "according to all that" are used of the builders of the tabernacle, who made everything as Yahweh had commanded Moses (Exodus 39:42). Here the priest builds by the king's command, from a pattern that came from Damascus (verse 10).

decisions.choice: had it finished by the time ... came back / finished it before ... came home
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly what "so he did until the king came" means (m1). Readable also says "the model and plan" for "all that the king had sent" (verse 10).

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֤א הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ מִדַּמֶּ֔שֶׂק וַיַּ֥רְא הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶת־הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חַ וַיִּקְרַ֥ב הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ וַיַּ֥עַל עָלָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And came the king from Damascus, and saw the king the altar, and drew near the king to the altar, and he offered up on it.

en.L: And the king came from Damascus, and the king saw the altar, and the king drew near to the altar and offered [sacrifices] on it.
en.B: On his return from Damascus the king saw the altar; he approached it and offered sacrifices on it.
en.R: The king came home from Damascus and saw the altar. He went up to it and offered sacrifices on it.

es.L: Y vino el rey de Damasco, y el rey vio el altar, y el rey se acercó al altar y ofreció [sacrificios] sobre él.
es.B: Cuando el rey volvió de Damasco, vio el altar; se acercó a él y ofreció sacrificios sobre él.
es.R: El rey regresó de Damasco y vio el altar. Se acercó a él y ofreció sacrificios sobre él.

fr.L: Et le roi revint de Damas, et le roi vit l’autel, et le roi s’approcha de l’autel et y offrit [des sacrifices].
fr.B: À son retour de Damas, le roi vit l’autel ; il s’en approcha et y offrit des sacrifices.
fr.R: Le roi est rentré de Damas et il a vu l’autel. Il s’en est approché et il y a offert des sacrifices.

sw.L: Naye mfalme akaja kutoka Dameski, naye mfalme akaiona madhabahu, naye mfalme akaikaribia madhabahu, akatoa [dhabihu] juu yake.

sw.R: Mfalme alirudi nyumbani kutoka Dameski, akaiona madhabahu. Akaikaribia, akatoa dhabihu juu yake.

ko.L: 그리고 왕이 다메섹에서 와서, 왕이 그 제단을 보았다. 그리고 왕이 그 제단에 가까이 가서 그 위에 [제물을] 바쳤다.

pt.R: O rei voltou de Damasco e viu o altar. Ele foi até o altar e ofereceu sacrifícios sobre ele.

decisions.choice: offered on it: or "went up on it"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew letters can be read as "he went up on it", climbing the altar's steps or ramp, or as "he offered up on it", making offerings rise on it. The vowels of the Hebrew text give "offered up", and verse 13 says what he offered. Either way Ahaz himself served at the altar.

decisions.choice: the king at the altar: Ahaz acts as priest
decisions.reason: The word "king" is repeated three times: it is the king who sees, approaches and offers. Kings had offered sacrifices at great occasions before (1 Kings 8:62-64), but Jeroboam's offering at his own altar is the closest parallel (1 Kings 12:33). 2 Chronicles 26:16-21 tells how Uzziah was struck with skin disease for burning incense in the temple.

decisions.choice: On his return ... the king saw the altar; he approached it ... / The king came home ... He went up to it ...
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable join the four short clauses into fewer sentences and say "the king" once. Literal keeps the repetition.

decisions.choice: sacrifices
decisions.reason: The verb has no object; English needs one. Literal puts it in brackets.

decisions.choice: burnt, grain, drink and peace offerings: the offerings that dedicate an altar
decisions.reason: These are the main kinds of offering in the law (Leviticus 1-3; Numbers 15:1-10). Offered together, they put the new altar into use, as Solomon's offerings did at the dedication of the temple (1 Kings 8:64).

decisions.choice: his ... which were his: the king's own offerings
decisions.reason: Each offering is called "his", and the peace offerings "which were his". These were the king's own offerings, not the people's.

decisions.choice: dashed: threw the blood against the altar
decisions.reason: The verb means to throw or splash a liquid. The blood of the offerings was thrown against the altar (Leviticus 3:2).

decisions.choice: dashed (Literal); splashed (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "splashed", as Leviticus 3:2 does; Literal keeps "dashed". Readable adds "on it" after the first clause so that every offering is placed on the new altar.

decisions.choice: "holocausto", "ofrenda de cereal", "libación" (L, B), "ofrenda de vino" (R), "sacrificios de paz"
decisions.reason: The names of the offerings as the Pentateuch terms note and the published Spanish Pentateuch set them; Readable says what the drink offering was.

decisions.choice: "roció"
decisions.reason: "Rociar" for the blood thrown against the altar at every level, as English Balanced and Readable say "splashed" (m3).

decisions.choice: "holocauste", "offrande végétale", "libation", "sacrifices de communion"
decisions.reason: The French names of the offerings set in the Pentateuch note and the Kings terms note, at every level.

decisions.choice: sadaka ya kuteketezwa, sadaka ya nafaka, sadaka ya kinywaji, sadaka za amani
decisions.reason: The names of the offerings as the published Swahili Leviticus and Numbers have them.

decisions.choice: "번제물", "곡식 제물", "부어 드리는 제물", "화목제물"
decisions.reason: "번제" and "화목제" are the settled terms of the earlier notes; for the grain and drink offerings Korean uses descriptive words a reader understands rather than the Sino-Korean church terms.

decisions.choice: của lễ thiêu; tế lễ chay; lễ quán; tế lễ bình an
decisions.reason: The offerings keep one name each: "tế lễ bình an" as the terms note sets for peace offerings, and the familiar "của lễ thiêu", "tế lễ chay" and "lễ quán" for the others.

decisions.choice: holocausto, oferta de cereal, oferta de bebida, sacrifícios de comunhão; lançou (L), jogou (B, R)
decisions.reason: The offerings (m1) take the words the Old Testament terms set for them, and "oferta de bebida" as Numbers 28:7 has it in Portuguese. The blood thrown against the altar (m3) is "lançar" at Literal and "jogar" at Balanced and Readable, as Leviticus 3:2 has it in Portuguese; "aspergir" would suggest a sprinkling.

decisions.choice: "የሚቃጠል መሥዋዕት", "የእህል ቁርባን", "የመጠጥ ቁርባን", "የኅብረት መሥዋዕት"
decisions.reason: The names of the offerings as Leviticus has them in Amharic.

decisions.choice: "होमबलि", "अन्नबलि", "अर्घ", "मेलबलि"
decisions.reason: The offerings keep the Pentateuch's terms, so the reader sees that Ahaz performs at the new altar the full service of Leviticus.

decisions.choice: Offering names as LEV and 1KI 9:25: "焼き尽くすささげ物" (L, B) / "焼いてささげるいけにえ" (R); "穀物のささげ物"; "注ぎの供え物"; shelamim "和解のいけにえ" (L), "交わりのいけにえ" (B, R); zaraq "振りかける"
decisions.reason: Settled terms for the whole OT.

decisions.choice: "всепалення", "хлібна жертва", "жертва виливання", "мирні жертви"
decisions.reason: The terms note and Ukrainian Leviticus name the offerings this way, so the altarʼs dedication reads with the words of the law.
